q1.boundary: The boundary of the Catalog Management bounded context (catalog-management) becomes a broker boundary. Its two services produce and consume on Apache Kafka (kafka:29092). Every other service stays on Redpanda (redpanda:29092). Event bindings that cross the context boundary now also cross the Kafka/Redpanda boundary, and MirrorMaker 2 bridges them in one direction per topic.

q4.must_preserve: The product read model must keep receiving ProductUpdated/ProductDeleted from catalog-service and ProductImagePromoted from image-service, both now produced on Kafka. The kafka->redpanda flow must deliver them under the same topic name, per product_id key in order, with headers intact. Otherwise storefront product data and image URLs go stale.

Attribute updates must still reach the product read model on Redpanda through the kafka->redpanda flow under the unchanged topic name. AIP has no catalog promise for this binding, so only the observed attachment shows it exists.
CategoryUpdated events must keep reaching the category read model on Redpanda through the kafka->redpanda flow, under the same topic name and in order.

Attribute updates must keep reaching the category read model on Redpanda through the kafka->redpanda flow. The binding is undeclared (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING), so a plan built only from declared bindings would leave it out.

Catalog-service on Kafka must keep receiving TenantUpdated and TenantDeleted from tenant-service, which stays on Redpanda, through the redpanda->kafka flow. Its consumer position must carry over (committed offset 1, set explicitly in P09). Skipping an event misses a tenant DB migration or cleanup; replaying one re-runs migrations or cleanup.

The same as for catalog-service: image-service must keep receiving tenant lifecycle events through the redpanda->kafka flow, and keep its offset (1). This drives tenant migrations and the S3 tenant cleaner, which wipes the tenant's image prefix when a tenant is deleted.

q5.statement: The evidence does not establish that events are delivered between the brokers. MirrorMaker 2 is at-least-once: the move is not lossless or exactly-once, and duplicates on Redpanda are possible. After the move, verify that end offsets on Kafka and on Redpanda grow together for the three catalog.* topics, and that tenant.tenant.events on Kafka keeps up with Redpanda.

q5.statement: An attachment is not event handling. Which event types each consumer actually handles is not established, and producers are declared only, never observed. Whether some other, undeclared producer writes catalog.* on Redpanda is unknown. If one exists, image-service on Kafka would no longer see its catalog.product.events records, because there is no reverse mirror.

The consumer picture is a point in time: AIP at 2026-10-29T20:02:22Z, covering only configured groups, and R1. A consumer added later would be missed. P02 re-checks the consumer groups right before the cutover.

The Helm values and topic configs were not available (R2). Still unverified: the exact values file paths and the key that sets the broker address; the auto-offset-reset, group-id and enable-dlq settings in the cluster; the partition counts (1 is inferred from R1) and the cleanup/retention configs. If DLQ is enabled, catalog.product.events.dlq or tenant.tenant.events.dlq would be written on Kafka and not mirrored. R1 shows no Redpanda group consuming any .dlq topic. P01 and P10 must verify these.

The inside binding ecommerce-image-service x catalog.product.events cannot be bridged into Kafka, because the topic is mirrored Kafka->Redpanda. Its continuity depends on draining image-service on Redpanda (P08) and starting its Kafka group at offset 0 of the new topic (P09). After the move, verify that image-service consumes the ProductUpdated events from the functional test and emits ProductImagePromoted.

Offsets are not guaranteed to line up between Redpanda and the mirrored Kafka topic. Setting tenant.tenant.events offsets to 1 is valid only if P06 shows equal end offsets. AIP's broker_id kafka:sokol111-local is the declared id of the current Redpanda broker, and AIP has no evidence about the new Apache Kafka broker. After the move, ask for the functional test and check that all crossing consumer groups are Stable with lag 0 on their brokers.
